doc.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Writing 'Flyin' Home' on the plane to Atlantic City
summary: Hampton tells how he hummed the melody of 'Flyin' Home' on his first flight, with Goodman's band heading to the Steel Pier.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When was the first time you recorded, or when did you write the tune “Flyin’ Home?” Do you remember that?

Yes, I wrote that “Flyin’ Home” we were in California with Benny Goodman’s band playing engagements out there, and all at once while we was out there in California, we got notice from the booking office, Benny did, that they wanted him in Atlantic City for a tremendous amount of money. They wanted him to play on the Steel Pier. And then Benny didn’t have no way to get there but to fly, to fly his whole aggregation there. And so none of us had flown on a plane before. So I was sitting there next to Benny and I kept humming this song, the melody of “Flyin’ Home.” So Benny said, “well what’s that
you’re humming?” I said, “I’m just making it up to keep myself amused.” I never flew before, and I’m trying to keep myself company.
